lines: Good work has a clean finish. Getting me home counts.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I count that as good work.
The road was rough, but you got me through it safely.
I never thought my own workshop door would look so welcoming.
You kept watch while I slept. I noticed.
We made it back without losing anyone or anything important.
I had doubts when we left. You answered most of them on the road.
My boots need repair, but the rest of me is sound.
You chose the safe path when the shorter one looked worse.
I am glad I trusted you with the journey.
The village bell sounded better than music when we returned.
You did not rush me when I needed a rest.
I expected trouble. I did not expect you to handle it so well.
Give me a day at the bench and I will feel like myself again.
The trip ended better than it began. Thank you for that.
You brought me all the way home. I will remember it.
I can complain about the road now because we survived it cleanly.
Next time you need someone along, ask me after my feet recover.
We are safe, we are home, and that is enough for tonight.
That trip handled poorly. I felt every bad turn on the way back.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer wounds and better choices.
I am grateful to be home. I am not ready to call the journey a success.
The healer says I will recover. That does not make this hurt less.
You got me back alive, though only just.
I should not have needed bandages before we reached the village.
Every step home reminded me where the plan went wrong.
My tools weigh nothing compared with this bruised shoulder.
I trusted you to keep the danger farther away than that.
We need to discuss the choices that left me injured once I can stand without swaying.
I am home because you helped. I am hurt because the trip went badly.
Do not ask me to travel again until these cuts close.
The road left marks I will be explaining for a while.
I kept moving because stopping out there felt worse.
You carried my pack after I was hit. I will give you that.
I need a healer before I need an apology.
We survived, but I will not pretend we handled it well.
Let me sit down before we decide what this journey meant.
Next time, turn back before the danger costs this much.
A tool used wrong can still be repaired. Trust is less forgiving.
Following you was trust. What you did afterward was betrayal.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
You brought me out there knowing I had put my safety in your hands.
I watched the road for enemies. I should have watched you.
Do not call it a mistake. You chose to hurt me.
Getting home did not undo your betrayal.
I will mend the wound myself. Stay away from the rest.
You knew I was depending on you and used that against me.
I am back in the village, but I do not feel safe around you.
The bruise will fade before the memory does.
I trusted your directions, your promises, and your back. Never again.
No repair at my bench starts with pretending the break never happened.
Do not ask for forgiveness while I am still bleeding.
You turned a hard journey into something I cannot excuse.
I would rather walk alone than follow you again.
The village may hear your version. I know where the blow came from.
Keep your distance until I decide what comes next.
You did not just hurt me. You made every kindness on that trip feel false.
Trust is not a handle I can simply replace.
That boat was the right tool for the crossing. I will give you that.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding about the rest of the plan.
The water carried us home faster than the road would have.
I was glad to see the dock, even if my legs had forgotten solid ground.
You kept the bow straight when the current pulled at us.
The boat leaked less than I feared and splashed more than I wanted.
I owe that little hull more respect than I gave it at the start.
We reached home wet, tired, and safe enough.
Next time, let me wrap my tools before we launch.
You handled the oars well. I handled the seat with both hands.
The river shortened the journey and lengthened my list of worries.
I can still feel the dock moving under my feet.
Our landing was not graceful, but it was on the correct bank.
I thought the rapids would shake every rivet out of my pack.
You found a calm channel when I could not see one.
I would take that boat again after someone checks the seams.
The crossing went better once I stopped watching the water below us.
We made good time whenever the wind agreed.
I did not enjoy the waves, but I trusted your steering.
Home by boat still counts as home.
